acceptance_criteria.criterion: All previously passing validator tests continue to pass

summary: Fixed isValidStatusTransition() self-transition guard: changed `if (from === to) return true` to `return from !== 'CANCELLED'` so CANCELLED→CANCELLED is rejected (terminal status).
Added IN_PROGRESS→READY transition to isValidStatusTransition() case 'IN_PROGRESS' (unclaim path, spec §21.13).
Added COMPLETE→CANCELLED transition to isValidStatusTransition() case 'COMPLETE' (PM-only path).
Updated getLegalTransitions() in work-package.ts: IN_PROGRESS now lists READY, COMPLETE now lists CANCELLED.
Updated UpdateWorkPackageStatusSchema .describe() string to document all new legal transitions.
Updated JSDoc comment in validators.ts to document new transitions.

Updated validators.test.ts: renamed same-status no-op test, flipped IN_PROGRESS→READY expectation, added CANCELLED→CANCELLED rejected test, added CANCELLED→any rejected test, added COMPLETE→CANCELLED allowed test.
Updated cancelled-status.test.ts: flipped COMPLETE→CANCELLED test from false to true per spec.
All 624 tests pass, 0 TypeScript errors.

comments.note: tests/tools/cancelled-status.test.ts contained a test asserting COMPLETE→CANCELLED is NOT valid, which contradicts the spec. This pre-existing test was silently masking the missing transition. Consider adding a manifest note or test comment explaining the spec rationale (PM-only cancellation of complete WPs) to prevent future regressions.

The `getLegalTransitions()` helper in work-package.ts is duplicated from the switch in `isValidStatusTransition()`. A derived approach (querying the validator for each target status) would eliminate drift risk, but the current duplication is low-risk given the small enum size.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified against source code and live test execution.

comments.note: COMPLETE→COMPLETE same-status returns true (no-op) — consistent with spec's 'non-CANCELLED statuses allow self-transitions as no-ops'. Low risk.
No observations — code is clean and consistent. Implementation aligns with JSDoc, test names include spec reference (§21.13), and COMPLETE→CANCELLED test comment documents PM-only rationale clearly.

summary: Reviewed validators.ts, work-package.ts, validators.test.ts, and cancelled-status.test.ts.
The self-transition guard refactor (`return from !== 'CANCELLED'`) is correct and elegant — single-point-of-change for the no-op rule without duplicating the terminal check.
getLegalTransitions() helper is in sync with isValidStatusTransition() for all new transitions (IN_PROGRESS→READY, COMPLETE→CANCELLED).
The UpdateWorkPackageStatusSchema .describe() string fully documents all new legal transitions including the new paths.
Test coverage is thorough: each new transition has a positive test, each rejected path has a negative test, and the CANCELLED self-transition rejection is explicitly isolated.
No blocking issues found. Code is maintainable, correct, and consistent with the JSDoc and spec references.

comments.note: getLegalTransitions() in work-package.ts is a string-formatting helper that duplicates the switch logic from isValidStatusTransition(). It's only used in error messages so drift risk is low, but a future refactor deriving it from the validator (e.g., iterating WorkPackageStatus values and calling isValidStatusTransition) would make this zero-drift. Not blocking — low enum size makes manual sync acceptable.

The self-transition guard `return from !== 'CANCELLED'` elegantly handles the non-CANCELLED no-op case but relies on the reader understanding that CANCELLED is the only terminal self-transition-rejected status. The existing JSDoc comment on isValidStatusTransition covers this, so it's fine. No action required.

No observations — code is clean and consistent. All changes are minimal, targeted, and correctly scoped to the acceptance criteria. Pre-existing test-masking issue was caught and corrected (cancelled-status.test.ts COMPLETE→CANCELLED flip).
